newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AssiDoman to buy Slovakian paper plant.
newsitem.headline: AssiDoman to buy Slovakian paper plant.

text.p: Swedish forestry company AssiDoman AB said on Monday it had reached an agreement with a number of shareholders to buy a majority of shares in Slovakian paper and paperboard company JCP Sturovo.
AssiDoman said it had also made a public offer for the remaining outstanding shares, intending at very soon exceeding a 90 percent share.

The company said in a statement that the JCP Sturovo, which is situated on the Danube near the Hungarian border, was a profitable company with strong market positions and an annual turnover of about 700 million crowns.
JCP Sturovo, with 2,500 staff, makes SC-fluting (the middle layer in corrugated board), corrugated board, carton board and asphalt-impregnated paper products.
The fluting mill has an annual capacity of 180,00 tonnes with 75 percent of output sold externally to the Czech Republic, Germany, Italy, Spain and Turkey among others.

AssiDoman said the corrugated packaging plant makes aobut 70 million square metres a year, making JCP Sturovo the largest corrugated producer in Slovakia. About 70 percent of this is sold in Slovakia, the rest mainly in Hungary, the Czech Republic, Poland and the Ukraine.

The output of asphalt-impregnated products amounts to 50 million square metres a year making JCP Sturovo the largest maker in Europe where total consumption is estimated at 800-900 million square metres a year.

"JCP Sturovo gives AssiDoman very interesting opportunities for development on the rapidly growing corrugated packaging markets in central and eastern Europe," AssiDoman's chief executive Lennart Ahlgren said in the statement.
"The company also fits in very well with our other investments in the region."
